query: measured latency cost of methods for For each synchronized detection and depth pair, send through stage 2 only the pallet select_detection already chooses, and mark every other candidate deferred by publishing its source index on the pose diagnostics together with that pair's RGB and depth capture stamps. The handling process can then tell which pallets in the still-changing scene were detected but not posed. on src
findings: Each detection sent through stage 2 pays another chamfer search. Liu, Tuzel, Veeraraghavan, and Chellappa (CVPR 2010) measured classic chamfer at 17.59 µs per hypothesis and oriented chamfer at 51.50 µs, mean over templates of 1,610 points; directional chamfer was 0.40 µs. Classic chamfer grows linearly with template points. Their directional matcher evaluated 1.05 million hypotheses in 0.42 s, and one object's 3D pose took 0.71 s that way against 29.1 s for classic chamfer and 65.3 s for oriented chamfer. In src, estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2 uses the default pocket prototype: contour spacing 0.03 m gives 182 points (outer 94, two pockets 44 each). The free search is the coarse grid 31×31×21 = 20,181 plus the fine grid 25×25×13 = 8,125, 28,306 hypotheses. The prior search runs when free cost is above 0.006233 m, because prior_lambda 3.0 times (1 − confidence) then exceeds lambda_floor 0.05, and that adds 21×21×21 = 9,261 plus another 8,125 (45,692 hypotheses in all). Scaling their 17.59 µs by 182/1,610 is about 1.99 µs per hypothesis, a serial envelope of about 56 ms for the free grids and about 91 ms if the prior grids also run. The search loop is OpenMP, so wall time is below that serial envelope. This scale is not a clock of pallet_pose_cpp_node. A deferred source index does not enter the search.

Posing every detection with a learned refiner has the same per-object multiplier. Labbé, Carpentier, Aubry, and Sivic (CosyPose, ECCV 2020) measured 190 ms to pose all candidates for 4 views and 6 detections per view, one coarse iteration and one refinement iteration, inside a 320 ms scene (association 40 ms, scene refinement 90 ms). CRT-6D reports that CosyPose pair at about 100 ms for a single object, and DeepIM at 41 ms per object per iteration. MegaPose measures one refiner iteration at about 50 ms on an RTX 2080, and 520 coarse hypotheses at about 2.5 s per object. FoundationPose measures 1.3 s per object on an i9-10980XE and RTX 3090 (init 4 ms, refinement 0.88 s, selection 0.42 s); tracking is about 32 Hz and still one object. select_detection already chooses one pallet; the others stay deferred.

The distance image is the cheap part of that per-detection cost, and an ICP substitute for the deferred pallets is not. OpenCV pull 28636, Jetson Orin geometric mean: 640×480 DIST_L2 DIST_MASK_PRECISE CV_32F is 0.718 ms on 4.x and 0.726 ms with the patch; DIST_L2 DIST_MASK_5 CV_32F on the same size is 3.217 ms on 4.x and 2.583 ms with the patch. src calls cv::distanceTransform with DIST_L2 and DIST_MASK_PRECISE once inside each estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2. Holzer, Hinterstoisser, Ilic, and Navab (CVPR 2009) measured distance-transform templates at about 0.15 s against exhaustive edge template matching at about 1.0 s on 1280×960, scale range 0.9 to 1.9. Open3D pull 3019 measured legacy point-to-plane ICP at 4.58 ms CPU for one iteration on 4,760 source and 3,440 target points at voxel 0.05. The same pull's 30-iteration legacy point-to-plane benchmark, after a 0.01 downsample to 95,354 and 63,857 points, is 749 ms CPU on an i7-7700HQ. Deferred candidates skip both the distance image and the grid.

Marking the other candidates is a few extra key/value strings on the DiagnosticArray this node already publishes for that pair, which already carries the RGB and depth capture stamps. It is not a second topic. Kronauer, Pohlmann, Matthé, Meissner, and Fettweis (arXiv:2101.02074, ROS 2 Foxy, desktop PC) measured the same latency at 128 B, 1 KB, and 10 KB; it rose at 100 KB and 500 KB, past the 64 KB UDP fragment. At 128 B, ROS 2 added up to 50% over raw DDS, from DDS and the rclcpp notification delay. Yu's ROS2-pubsub-benchmark, same-process ROS 2 C++ P90 per hop on an i7-9700K, is 113 µs at 100 Hz and 138 µs at 1 kHz for a small message. Fast DDS CDR (rosidl_typesupport_fastrtps pull 150, mean of three runs, pinned core) serializes a trivial String in 10.7 ns, a Header in 14.3 ns, and a Pose in 14.9 ns; the non-inlined Marker mean is 394 ns. diagnostic_msgs/DiagnosticStatus.values is a KeyValue array, and each KeyValue is two strings, so a few source-index pairs are tens of nanoseconds on the message already published. The stall cited by the ROS 2 DDS tuning guide, and by Cyclone DDS issue 346, is a large array of non-primitives: under Galactic, publish could not hold 1,000 Hz once a message held 5,000 elements that each contained a builtin_interfaces/Time. One index string per deferred candidate is the small side of that split.
